text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- National carrier Kenya Airways cancels three local flights and at least four international flights because of a pilots strike.
- President Daniel arap Moi says the government is working on a policy paper to "fully" commercialise the agricultural sector.
- U.S. Ambassador to Kenya Prudence Bushnell calls on the government to review its policies on media liberalisation.
- Parliament business is adjourned after a motion on Kenya Cooperative Creameries fails to appear on the order paper.
- Over 10,000 Kenyans have lost their jobs as a result of the restrictive qoutas on Kenya's exports of woven shirts and pillow cases into the United States market.
- In Central Province, livestock personnel confirm Nyahururu town and its environs has been hit by an epidemic of rabies.
- The Government moves swiftly to quash the city council "coup" staged on Tuesday to give Nairobi Mayor Dick Waweru executive powers.
- Members of Parliament from famine-stricken North Eastern Province appeal to the government to declare the area a disaster zone because of drought.
